root_cause.text: In `net/ipv6/ip6_fib.c:fib6_add_rt2node()`, the ECMP qualification logic dereferenced `iter->fib6_nh` without first ensuring the `fib6_info` instance actually had a trailing `struct fib6_nh`, which is not guaranteed for routes created with `RTA_NH_ID`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to `(iter->nh || !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family)`, and the CVE description states that when an IPv6 route is created with `RTA_NH_ID`, `struct fib6_info` “does not have the trailing struct fib6_nh,” making the original `iter->fib6_nh` read an out-of-bounds access; it also notes that `if iter->nh is not NULL, rt6_qualify_for_ecmp() returns false anyway`, so the missing `iter->nh` check was the unsafe condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust fib6 route flag clearing logic to handle nexthop-based entries correctly.
intent_record.what: In fib6_add_rt2node(), the condition guarding the clearing of RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT was changed from checking only !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family to checking (iter->nh || !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family).
intent_record.how: This broadens the cases in which the flags are cleared: existing nexthop-based entries now satisfy the condition even if fib_nh_gw_family is set, while non-nexthop entries still require a zero gateway family. As a result, route flag state is updated more accurately for nexthop-backed routes.

grouping_result.intent: Adjust fib6 route flag clearing logic to handle nexthop-based entries correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets nexthop-based fib6 entries, which is directly related to the root cause involving unsafe access to fib6_nh for routes created with RTA_NH_ID.

candidates.rationale: This condition leads directly to the dereference of iter->fib6_nh in the same ECMP qualification path; the vulnerable logic assumes fib6_nh is present without first verifying that the fib6_info instance has a trailing fib6_nh, which is unsafe for RTA_NH_ID routes.
This is the direct dereference of iter->fib6_nh that can fault when the fib6_info does not actually contain a trailing struct fib6_nh, which is the root cause described for RTA_NH_ID routes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional begins the ECMP qualification path that proceeds to dereference iter->fib6_nh without first confirming the fib6_info instance actually has a trailing struct fib6_nh, which is unsafe for RTA_NH_ID routes.
This is the direct dereference of iter->fib6_nh that can occur even when the fib6_info object lacks a trailing fib6_nh, matching the root cause for routes created with RTA_NH_ID.
